title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the Committee’s 2020 report on AI and Public Standards, outlining its plans to improve safety, transparency, and accountability for AI systems. It also introduces new rules and partnership programs to work with businesses and citizens, ensuring AI technologies serve the public interest.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is creating rules to guide how artificial intelligence can be used in exams and other qualifications, aiming to keep assessments fair, reliable, and secure. They will set clear guidelines for schools and testing bodies, monitor AI tools for bias or cheating, and enforce standards so learners’ achievements remain trustworthy.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyrighted works are used in training and operating AI systems and evaluates the legal and ethical implications of this practice. It offers recommendations for policymakers and industry stakeholders to balance the benefits of AI development with the protection of creators’ rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has issued a reply to the House of Lords AI report, saying it takes seriously the call for urgent action on artificial intelligence. It outlines plans for new rules, more research funding, public engagement and international partnership, stressing that the country cannot afford to be complacent about AI’s impact.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: The document sets out the terms of reference for a committee reviewing how artificial intelligence aligns with public standards, detailing its purpose, scope, and responsibilities. It also includes a FAQ section to help stakeholders understand the committee’s review process and key questions.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of artificial intelligence, highlighting its concerns and recommendations. The submission aims to inform lawmakers about best practices and regulatory approaches for AI oversight.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The policy explains how AI technologies will change the rules for approving and monitoring medical products, focusing on safety, effectiveness, and patient data protection. It outlines steps to apply the principles of the AI White Paper—such as transparency, accountability, and risk assessment—to create clear, adaptable guidelines for regulators, manufacturers, and healthcare providers.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy outlines how the organisation plans to become the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential defence body in the field of AI, given its size. It details a vision of leading AI innovation and application to strengthen national security and operational excellence.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Department for Transport (DfT) will collaborate with the transport sector to leverage the benefits of artificial intelligence, aiming to improve services and efficiency across the industry. At the same time, it will put measures in place to identify, manage, and mitigate any risks associated with deploying AI technologies.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: The report outlines how copyright‑protected works are being used to train and improve AI models, evaluating compliance with the Data (Use and Access) Act’s Section 137. It highlights progress made, identifies challenges such as licensing gaps and data quality, and offers recommendations for balancing intellectual property rights with AI innovation.
